intro: Welcome back! Today's lesson is about pronouns — short words like I, you, he, she and they that replace names, plus my, your and her for things that belong to people. Indonesian uses 'dia' for both he and she, so English needs a little extra care here. Warm-up: what word do you use in English to talk about yourself?
teachingNotes: Indonesian 'dia' maps to he OR she (and 'it' for things) — the most common error is mixing he/she.
Possessives come BEFORE the noun in English: my book (buku saya). Learners often reverse this.
Keep sentences very short; avoid verb tenses beyond 'is/are' used in examples.

keyPoints.title: Subject pronouns
keyPoints.explanation: I, you, he (a man/boy), she (a woman/girl), it (a thing or animal), we, they. Use them in place of a name at the start of a sentence.

examples.en: Andi is my friend. He is tall.
Rina is a doctor. She is kind.

keyPoints.title: Possessive adjectives
keyPoints.explanation: my, your, his, her, its, our, their show who owns something. They go BEFORE the noun.

examples.en: Budi and Sari love their cat.
examples.id: Budi dan Sari menyayangi kucing mereka.

keyPoints.title: Replacing nouns
keyPoints.explanation: One person: he or she. One thing: it. Two or more people or things: they. You + me: we.

examples.en: The phone is new. It is black.
My parents are at home. They are happy.
examples.id: Orang tua saya di rumah. Mereka senang.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rina is a teacher. ___ is friendly. (Which pronoun?)
Complete: I have a car. This is ___ car.
Replace the words in capitals with a pronoun: THE BOOKS are on the table.

independentPractice.prompt: Andi and I are students. ___ are in class. (Which pronoun?)
Complete: Budi has a dog. ___ dog is small.
independentPractice.hint: The dog belongs to a man.

assessment.prompt: My brother is 20. ___ is a student. (Write the pronoun.)
Sari and Dewi are sisters. ___ live in Bandung.
Complete: We have a new house. ___ house is big.
Rewrite with a pronoun for the words in capitals: THE COFFEE is hot.
assessment.rubric: Correct: It is hot. Accept just 'It'.
